target_customer: Small businesses, freelancers and founders needing a mobile first business bank account
problem: Small businesses were poorly served by traditional bank mobile and cash management tools.
business_model: Neobank layered on a partner bank, earning interchange and fees; later software licensing to banks

founders.name: Brian Merritt
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; later Head of Payments/BaaS at Cross River Bank after the Seed sale.

founders.name: Ryan Hildebrand
founders.background_notes: Per YC page, part of early Simple team and led its sale to BBVA.

competitors.name: Simple
competitors.what: Smartphone first consumer bank on a partner bank; Seed's founders came from it

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app and onboarding on top of a partner bank with compliance and KYC integration; standard fintech engineering with regulatory hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Built on a partner bank, so product was copyable and customers could switch accounts; the later onboarding system had value to banks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Seed wound down direct service in Nov 2018 and sold the platform and team to Cross River Bank in June 2019.

market_need_then: Seed pitched that banks failed small businesses on mobile and cash management (PYMNTS and TechCrunch 2015 coverage); demand was claimed rather than measured.

branding.domain_note: Used seed.co, a non-.com domain; the word Seed is shared by many unrelated brands.

brand_strength.rationale: Fits the start-a-business promise, but name searches mostly return other Seed brands and no brand press was found.

pivots.from: Direct consumer facing small business bank
pivots.to: Software licensing and services for banks and non-banks
pivots.why: Company email said it could not create a sustainable alternative to the big banks.

outcome_analysis: Seed was founded by two ex-Simple executives, raised about 5.2 million dollars with General Catalyst leading a roughly 5 million round in October 2015, then ended its direct banking offering in November 2018 saying it could not build a sustainable alternative to big banks. Cross River Bank bought the platform and team in June 2019, a soft landing; the exact economics are not public.
notes: Round stage is other because sources do not state a Series A label. Investor list is from the Crunchbase News article; the company's own Medium post on investors returned 403 and was not read, so the 5M figure rests on that one article plus aggregators (CB Insights total 5.12M). Earlier small seed amounts (120K YC, 650K) are aggregator only and unrecorded. Failure factor other: the stated cause was no sustainable alternative to big banks, which fits no taxonomy code cleanly. Competitor Simple is dated to the 2014 AP story; other small business neobanks launched later or were not dated. No logo or brand information found.
